svg.aria-label: How to write ۲ ۳: 2 digits, ۲, ۳, one after another
svg.title: Writing ۲ ۳
svg.desc: 2 digits written one after another: ۲, ۳ (perso-arabic). Each digit has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that digit, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished digit, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each digit is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the digits are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ۲: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 447 aligned samples of ۲ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 447 (100%); starts at the top right in 427 (96%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>; ۳: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 494 aligned samples of ۳ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 490 (99%); starts at the top right in 480 (97%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>. Source notes on variation: ۲: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 447 samples of ۲, 447 (100%) are one stroke. 427 (96%) start at the top right. Of the 447 one-stroke samples, 433 (97%) reach the top left after leaving the start, so the pen crosses the top from right to left and climbs into the stem's head, and 445 (100%) end in the bottom third: the stem comes last, downward. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer. ۳: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 494 samples of ۳, 490 (99%) are one stroke. 480 (97%) start at the top right. Of the 490 one-stroke samples, 472 (96%) reach the top left after leaving the start, so the pen crosses both teeth from right to left and climbs into the stem's head, and 488 (100%) end in the bottom third: the stem comes last, downward. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 digits, one after another
Digit 1 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Digit 2 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Digit 1: stroke order after POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039,
Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 447 aligned samples of ۲ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 447 (100%); starts at the top right in 427 (96%)
Digit 2: stroke order after POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039,
Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 494 aligned samples of ۳ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 490 (99%); starts at the top right in 480 (97%)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
